findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with only S3's default (SSE-S3) protection rather than a customer-managed KMS key. There is no enforced encryption policy and no opportunity to control key access, rotation, or revocation independently of S3.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with reports_archive, and no account-level restriction is visible. Any overly broad bucket policy or ACL added later would take effect immediately, so the bucket lacks a defence-in-depth guard against accidental public exposure.

force_destroy = true allows Terraform to delete the bucket and all archived reports without confirmation, including during an accidental destroy of the workspace. A failed or reverted apply can irreversibly destroy the retention record for this data.
ledger_exports contains financial ledger data but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving the data encrypted only with S3-managed keys and without a customer-controlled KMS key.

No public access block is attached to ledger_exports. Combined with an inline acl = "private" (which is also the deprecated bucket-level ACL form), there is nothing preventing a future ACL or policy from exposing ledger data publicly.
force_destroy = true permits the ledger export bucket and its contents to be deleted by Terraform without protection, removing financial records that may be subject to retention requirements.
model_artifacts stores model weights and training data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects rely on default S3-managed encryption with no customer-controlled key.
No public access block is associated with model_artifacts, so the bucket is not hardened against a policy or ACL change that would make model artifacts publicly readable.

ops_runbooks has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbooks (which typically contain internal procedures, endpoints, and credentials references) encrypted only with default S3-managed keys.
No public access block is attached to ops_runbooks, so the bucket lacks an account-level guard preventing future public exposure of internal runbook content.
force_destroy = true allows the runbook bucket and its contents to be destroyed by Terraform without safeguard.

audit_trail uses acl = "log-delivery-write", a legacy canned ACL that grants the log-delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP permissions on the bucket. Combined with lack of public access blocking, this widens the set of principals able to modify audit log content and metadata.
The audit trail bucket, which receives log deliveries from other buckets, has no public access block. Audit logs are high-value tamper targets and should be hardened against policy or ACL changes.
force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket means Terraform can delete the security audit record entirely, undermining the integrity and availability of the audit history.

reports_seed_object is uploaded without a kms_key_id or explicit SSE setting, relying on whatever default encryption applies to the target bucket. Since reports_archive declares no encryption configuration, the seeded vendor roster object is stored under S3-managed keys only.
